passages.text: When Jesus had finished saying all these things, He told His disciples, “You know that the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus finished saying all these things.
He spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You know the Passover is in two days.
The Son of Man will be handed over.
He will be crucified.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Οἴδατε ὅτι μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας τὸ πάσχα γίνεται καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς τὸ σταυρωθῆναι

passages.text: At that time the chief priests and elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas, and they conspired to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests led the people.
The elders of the people also led them.
They gathered together at that time.
They met in the courtyard of the high priest.
The high priest’s name was Caiaphas.
They made a secret plan together.
They wanted to arrest Jesus by trickery.
They planned to kill Jesus.
passages.original: Τότε συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τοῦ λεγομένου Καϊάφα καὶ συνεβουλεύσαντο ἵνα τὸν Ἰησοῦν δόλῳ κρατήσωσιν καὶ ἀποκτείνωσιν

passages.text: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and elders spoke together.
They said, “Not during the feast.”
They did not want trouble among the people.
They feared a riot might happen.
passages.original: ἔλεγον δέ Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ ἵνα μὴ θόρυβος γένηται ἐν τῷ λαῷ

passages.text: While Jesus was in Bethany in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came to Him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, which she poured on His head as He reclined at the table.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in Bethany.
He was in the house of Simon the Leper.
A woman came to Jesus.
She brought an alabaster jar.
The jar contained expensive perfume.
Jesus was reclining at the table.
The woman poured the perfume on Jesus’ head.
passages.original: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γενομένου ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου βαρυτίμου καὶ κατέχεεν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου

passages.text: When the disciples saw this, they were indignant and asked, “Why this waste?
passages.sermon: The disciples saw what the woman did.\r\nThey became indignant.\r\nThey asked, “Why this waste?”
passages.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἠγανάκτησαν λέγοντες Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη

passages.text: This perfume could have been sold at a high price, and the money given to the poor.”
passages.sermon:
The disciples saw the woman pour expensive perfume on Jesus’ head.
They felt upset.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “This perfume could have been sold for a lot of money.
The money could have been given to the poor.”
passages.original: ἐδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο πραθῆναι πολλοῦ καὶ δοθῆναι πτωχοῖς

passages.text: Aware of this, Jesus asked, “Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw what was happening.
Jesus understood the situation.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Why are you troubling this woman?”
This woman has done a good thing for Me.
passages.original: Γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί κόπους παρέχετε τῇ γυναικί ἔργον γὰρ καλὸν ἠργάσατο εἰς ἐμέ

passages.text: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “You will always have poor people with you.\r\nYou will not always have Me with you.”
passages.original: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε

passages.text: By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial.
passages.sermon: A woman poured perfume on Jesus.\r\nShe poured the perfume on His body.\r\nShe did this to prepare Jesus for burial.
passages.original: βαλοῦσα γὰρ αὕτη τὸ μύρον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματός μου πρὸς τὸ ἐνταφιάσαι με ἐποίησεν

passages.text: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
People will preach this gospel in all the world.
Wherever people preach this gospel, they will also speak about what this woman has done.
They will remember her by telling what she did.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ λαληθήσεται καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς

passages.text: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests and asked, “What are you willing to give me if I hand Him over to you?” And they set out for him thirty pieces of silver.
passages.sermon:
Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.
Judas went to the chief priests.
Judas spoke to the chief priests.
Judas asked, “What will you give me if I hand Jesus over to you?”
The chief priests offered Judas thirty pieces of silver.
passages.original: Τότε πορευθεὶς εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριώτης πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς εἶπεν Τί θέλετέ μοι δοῦναι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν οἱ δὲ ἔστησαν αὐτῷ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια

passages.text: So from then on Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples.
Judas went to the chief priests.
Judas agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
From that time, Judas looked for a chance to hand Jesus over to them.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπὸ τότε ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδῷ

passages.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus.
\r\nThe disciples wanted to serve Jesus.
\r\nThe Feast of Unleavened Bread began.
\r\nThis feast was important for the Jewish people.
\r\nOn the first day of the feast, the disciples approached Jesus.
\r\nThey spoke to Jesus.
\r\nThey asked Jesus a question.
\r\nThey said, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal for you?”
\r\nThe Passover meal was a special meal.
\r\nThe disciples wanted to prepare this meal for Jesus.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ πρώτῃ τῶν ἀζύμων προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες Ποῦ θέλεις ἑτοιμάσωμέν σοι φαγεῖν τὸ πάσχα

passages.text: He answered, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him that the Teacher says, ‘My time is near. I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “Go into the city.”
He told them to find a certain man.
He said, “Speak to that man.”
He told them what to say.
He said, “The Teacher says, ‘My time is near.’”
He said, “I will keep the Passover at your house.”
He said, “I will eat the Passover with My disciples.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν πρὸς τὸν δεῖνα καὶ εἴπατε αὐτῷ Ὁ Διδάσκαλος λέγει Ὁ καιρός μου ἐγγύς ἐστιν πρὸς σὲ ποιῶ τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου

passages.text: So the disciples did as Jesus had directed them and prepared the Passover.
passages.sermon: The disciples followed Jesus’ instructions.\r\nThey prepared the Passover meal.
passages.original: καὶ ἐποίησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὡς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα

passages.text: When evening came, Jesus was reclining with the twelve disciples.
passages.sermon: Jesus was with His twelve disciples.\r\nEvening came.\r\nJesus reclined at the table with them.
passages.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἀνέκειτο μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα μαθητῶν

passages.text: And while they were eating, He said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was eating with His twelve disciples.
They were sharing a meal together.
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “Truly, I tell you this.
One of you will betray Me.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με

passages.text: They were deeply grieved and began to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”
passages.sermon:
The twelve disciples sat with Jesus.
Jesus told them that one of them would betray Him.
The disciples felt very sad.
Each disciple spoke to Jesus.
Each disciple asked, “Surely not I, Lord?”
passages.original: Καὶ λυπούμενοι σφόδρα ἤρξαντο λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς ἕκαστος Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι Κύριε

passages.text: Jesus answered, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe answered their question.\r\nHe said, “The person who dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ὁ ἐμβάψας μετ’ ἐμοῦ τὴν χεῖρα ἐν τῷ τρυβλίῳ οὗτός με παραδώσει

passages.text: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed. It would be better for him if he had not been born.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
God wrote about the Son of Man in the Scriptures.
The Son of Man will go as the Scriptures say.
A man will betray the Son of Man.
Trouble will come to that man.
It would be better for that man if he had never been born.
passages.original: ὁ μὲν Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος

passages.text: Then Judas, who would betray Him, said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?” Jesus answered, “You have said it yourself.”
passages.sermon:
Judas was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Judas planned to betray Jesus.
Judas spoke to Jesus.
Judas said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?”
Jesus replied to Judas.
Jesus said, “You have said it yourself.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν εἶπεν Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι ῥαββί Λέγει αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶπας

passages.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is My body.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was eating with His disciples.
He took bread.
He spoke a blessing over the bread.
He broke the bread.
He gave the bread to the disciples.
He said, “Take and eat.
This is My body.”
passages.original: Ἐσθιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν λαβὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἄρτον καὶ εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ δοὺς τοῖς μαθηταῖς εἶπεν Λάβετε φάγετε τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου

passages.text: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat with His disciples.
Jesus took a cup.
Jesus gave thanks to God.
Jesus gave the cup to His disciples.
Jesus said, “All of you, drink from this cup.”
passages.original: Καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων Πίετε ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες

passages.text: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus held a cup.
Jesus said, “This is My blood.”
This blood belongs to the covenant.
My blood is poured out for many people.
My blood is given for the forgiveness of sins.
passages.original: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ περὶ πολλῶν ἐκχυννόμενον εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν

passages.text: I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “I tell you the truth.
I will not drink this fruit of the vine from now on.
I will wait until that day comes.
On that day, I will drink it new with you.
We will be together in My Father’s kingdom.”
passages.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπ’ ἄρτι ἐκ τούτου τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω μεθ’ ὑμῶν καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Πατρός μου

passages.text: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples finished the meal.
They sang a hymn together.
They left the place where they ate.
They went out to the Mount of Olives.
passages.original: Καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “This very night you will all fall away on account of Me. For it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Tonight, all of you will fall away because of Me.
Scripture says, ‘I will strike the Shepherd.
The sheep of the flock will be scattered.’”
passages.original: Τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πάντες ὑμεῖς σκανδαλισθήσεσθε ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ταύτῃ γέγραπται γάρ Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα Καὶ διασκορπισθήσονται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης

passages.text: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said He would rise from the dead.
Jesus said, "After I have risen, I will go ahead of you."
Jesus said He would go ahead of the disciples into Galilee.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν

passages.text: Peter said to Him, “Even if all fall away on account of You, I never will.”
passages.sermon: Peter was a disciple of Jesus.\r\nPeter spoke to Jesus.\r\nPeter said, “Even if everyone else falls away because of You, I will not fall away.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Εἰ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται ἐν σοί ἐγὼ οὐδέποτε σκανδαλισθήσομαι

passages.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus declared, “this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.”
Jesus said, “This very night, you will deny Me.”
Jesus said, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
passages.original: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με

passages.text: Peter replied, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the other disciples said the same thing.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “Even if I must die with You, I will not deny You.”
All the other disciples also spoke.
They said the same thing as Peter.
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος Κἂν δέῃ με σὺν σοὶ ἀποθανεῖν οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι ὁμοίως καὶ πάντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν

passages.text: At that time Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and He told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a teacher and leader.
He had disciples who followed Him.
At that time, Jesus went with His disciples.
They went to a place called Gethsemane.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, "Sit here."
He said, "I will go over there and pray."
passages.original: Τότε ἔρχεται μετ’ αὐτῶν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς χωρίον λεγόμενον Γεθσημανὶ καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς Καθίσατε αὐτοῦ ἕως οὗ ἀπελθὼν ἐκεῖ προσεύξωμαι

passages.text: He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee and began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples in Gethsemane.
He took Peter with Him.
He also took the two sons of Zebedee with Him.
Jesus began to feel sorrowful.
Jesus became deeply distressed.
passages.original: Καὶ παραλαβὼν τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου ἤρξατο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν

passages.text: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “My soul is full of sorrow.
I am sorrowful to the point of death.
Stay here.
Keep watch with Me.”
passages.original: τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: Going a little farther, He fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Yet not as I will, but as You will.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus went a little farther from His disciples.
He fell facedown on the ground.
He prayed to God the Father.
He said, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me.”
He also said, “Yet not as I will, but as You will.”
passages.original: Καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ προσευχόμενος καὶ λέγων Πάτερ μου εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν παρελθάτω ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλ’ ὡς σύ

passages.text: Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?” He asked Peter.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
\r\nJesus returned to His disciples.
\r\nHe found the disciples sleeping.
\r\nJesus spoke to Peter.
\r\nHe said, “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ Οὕτως οὐκ ἰσχύσατε μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to stay awake.
He told them to pray.
He said, “Do this so you will not enter into temptation.”
He explained, “The spirit wants to do what is right.”
He also said, “But the body is weak.”
passages.original: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής

passages.text: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
\r\nJesus went away from His disciples a second time.
\r\nJesus prayed to God the Father.
\r\nJesus said, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”
\r\nJesus accepted the Father’s will, even if it meant suffering.
passages.original: Πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο λέγων Πάτερ μου εἰ οὐ δύναται τοῦτο παρελθεῖν ἐὰν μὴ αὐτὸ πίω γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου

passages.text: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping—for their eyes were heavy.
passages.sermon: Jesus returned to His disciples.\r\nHe found them sleeping.\r\nTheir eyes were heavy with sleep.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν πάλιν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ βεβαρημένοι

passages.text: So He left them and went away once more and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
He was in the garden with His disciples.
He left His disciples again.
He went away from them.
He prayed a third time.
He said the same words as before.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο ἐκ τρίτου τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπὼν πάλιν

passages.text: Then He returned to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus returned to His disciples.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting?
Look.
The hour is near.
The Son of Man is being betrayed.
He is handed over to sinners.”
passages.original: τότε ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλῶν

passages.text: Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Get up.
Let us go.
Look.
The one who will betray Me is coming.”
passages.original: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ὁ παραδιδούς με

passages.text: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and elders of the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was still speaking.
Judas arrived.
Judas was one of the twelve disciples.
A large crowd came with Judas.
The crowd carried swords and clubs.
The chief priests sent the crowd.
The elders of the people also sent the crowd.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἦλθεν καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος πολὺς μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων ἀπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τοῦ λαοῦ

passages.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him.”
passages.sermon:
Judas was one of Jesus’ twelve disciples.
Judas decided to betray Jesus.
Judas made a plan with the men who came to arrest Jesus.
Judas gave them a signal.
Judas said, “The man I kiss is Jesus.”
Judas told them, “Arrest Him.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς σημεῖον λέγων Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν κρατήσατε αὐτόν

passages.text: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
passages.sermon:
Judas was one of the Twelve disciples.
Judas went straight to Jesus.
Judas said, “Greetings, Rabbi!”
Judas kissed Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ εὐθέως προσελθὼν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπεν Χαῖρε ῥαββί καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν

passages.text: “Friend,” Jesus replied, “do what you came for.” Then the men stepped forward, seized Jesus, and arrested Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Judas.
Jesus called Judas "Friend."
Jesus said, "Do what you came for."
The men approached Jesus.
The men laid their hands on Jesus.
The men seized Jesus.
The men arrested Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἑταῖρε ἐφ’ ὃ πάρει Τότε προσελθόντες ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν

passages.text: At this, one of Jesus’ companions drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
passages.sermon:
One man stood with Jesus.
This man was one of Jesus’ companions.
He reached out his hand.
He drew his sword.
He struck the servant of the high priest.
He cut off the servant’s ear.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς τῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπέσπασεν τὴν μάχαιραν αὐτοῦ καὶ πατάξας τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτίον

passages.text: “Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to his companion.\r\nJesus said, "Put your sword back in its place."\r\nEveryone who takes up the sword will die by the sword.
passages.original: Τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀπόστρεψον τὴν μάχαιράν σου εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς πάντες γὰρ οἱ λαβόντες μάχαιραν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀπολοῦνται

passages.text: Are you not aware that I can call on My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his companion.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus has great authority and power.
Jesus said, “Do you not know this?”
Jesus can call on His Father at any time.
God the Father is all-powerful.
If Jesus asks, the Father will send help immediately.
God can send more than twelve legions of angels to help Jesus.
A legion is a large group of angels.
God can send many angels to protect Jesus right away.
passages.original: ἢ δοκεῖς ὅτι οὐ δύναμαι παρακαλέσαι τὸν Πατέρα μου καὶ παραστήσει μοι ἄρτι πλείω δώδεκα λεγιῶνας ἀγγέλων

passages.text: But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that say it must happen this way?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciple.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “The Scriptures must be fulfilled.”
The Scriptures say these things must happen this way.
If I stopped this, the Scriptures would not be fulfilled.
Therefore, these events must happen as the Scriptures say.
passages.original: πῶς οὖν πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ ὅτι οὕτως δεῖ γενέσθαι

passages.text: At that time Jesus said to the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw? Every day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd at that time.
He said, "You have come out to arrest Me with swords and clubs.
You treat Me as if I am an outlaw.
Every day I sat in the temple courts.
I taught there.
You did not arrest Me then."
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς ὄχλοις Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐκαθεζόμην διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με

passages.text: But this has all happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The prophets wrote about Him long ago.
Everything that happened to Jesus fulfilled what the prophets wrote.
All these events took place to fulfill the Scriptures.
After this, all the disciples left Jesus.
They ran away from Him.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ τῶν προφητῶν Τότε οἱ μαθηταὶ πάντες ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον

passages.text: Those who had arrested Jesus led Him away to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
passages.sermon:
A group of men arrested Jesus.
These men took Jesus away.
They brought Jesus to the house of Caiaphas.
Caiaphas was the high priest.
The scribes had gathered at this house.
The elders had also gathered there.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ κρατήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήγαγον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα ὅπου οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι συνήχθησαν

passages.text: But Peter followed Him at a distance, right up to the courtyard of the high priest. And he went in and sat down with the guards to see the outcome.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter followed Jesus after He was arrested.
Peter did not walk close to Jesus.
Peter stayed far behind Jesus.
Peter followed Jesus until he reached the courtyard of the high priest.
Peter entered the courtyard.
Peter sat down with the guards.
Peter wanted to see what would happen to Jesus.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἕως τῆς αὐλῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ εἰσελθὼν ἔσω ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν ἰδεῖν τὸ τέλος

passages.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false testimony against Jesus in order to put Him to death.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests led the people of Israel in religious matters.
The Sanhedrin was the council of Jewish leaders.
The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin wanted to kill Jesus.
They looked for people to speak falsely against Jesus.
They searched for false testimony against Him.
They did this so they could put Jesus to death.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τὸ συνέδριον ὅλον ἐζήτουν ψευδομαρτυρίαν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν θανατώσωσιν

passages.text: But they did not find any, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward and declared, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin wanted to put Jesus to death.
They looked for false testimony against Jesus.
Many false witnesses came forward.
The leaders did not find any testimony that would help them.
At last, two men came forward.
These two men spoke about Jesus.
They said, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
passages.original: καὶ οὐχ εὗρον πολλῶν προσελθόντων ψευδομαρτύρων Ὕστερον δὲ προσελθόντες δύο εἶπαν Οὗτος ἔφη Δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν οἰκοδομῆσαι

passages.text: So the high priest stood up and asked Him, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
passages.sermon:
The high priest stood up.
He spoke to Jesus.
He asked Jesus a question.
He said, “Do you have no answer?”
He said, “What are these men testifying against you?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν

passages.text: But Jesus remained silent. Then the high priest said to Him, “I charge You under oath by the living God: Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the high priest.
Jesus did not speak.
The high priest spoke to Jesus.
The high priest said, “I put you under oath before the living God.
Tell us if you are the Christ.
Tell us if you are the Son of God.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα Καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἐξορκίζω σε κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος ἵνα ἡμῖν εἴπῃς εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: “You have said it yourself,” Jesus answered. “But I say to all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the high priest and the council.
The high priest asked Jesus if He was the Christ, the Son of God.
Jesus answered the high priest directly.
Jesus said, “You have said it.”
Jesus continued to speak to everyone present.
Jesus said, “From now on, you will see the Son of Man.”
The Son of Man will sit at the right hand of Power.
The Son of Man will come on the clouds of heaven.
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Σὺ εἶπας πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπ’ ἄρτι ὄψεσθε τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “He has blasphemed! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.
passages.sermon:
The high priest heard Jesus speak.
The high priest tore his clothes.
He said, “He has blasphemed!”
He asked, “Why do we need any more witnesses?”
He said, “Now you have heard the blasphemy.”
passages.original: Τότε ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς διέρρηξεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ λέγων Ἐβλασφήμησεν τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων ἴδε νῦν ἠκούσατε τὴν βλασφημίαν

passages.text: What do you think?” “He deserves to die,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
The high priest spoke to the people.
He asked, "What do you think?"
The people answered him.
They said, "He deserves to die."
passages.original: τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ Οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν Ἔνοχος θανάτου ἐστίν

passages.text: Then they spit in His face and struck Him. Others slapped Him and said, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit You?”
passages.sermon:
The men stood before Jesus.
They spit in His face.
They struck Him with their fists.
Others slapped Him.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Prophesy to us, Christ!”
They asked, “Who hit You?”
passages.original: Τότε ἐνέπτυσαν εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκολάφισαν αὐτόν οἱ δὲ ἐράπισαν λέγοντες Προφήτευσον ἡμῖν Χριστέ τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε

passages.text: Meanwhile, Peter was sitting out in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him. “You also were with Jesus the Galilean,” she said.
passages.sermon:
Peter was outside.
He sat in the courtyard.
A servant girl came to Peter.
She spoke to him.
She said, “You were with Jesus the Galilean.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐκάθητο ἔξω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ καὶ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ μία παιδίσκη λέγουσα Καὶ σὺ ἦσθα μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Γαλιλαίου

passages.text: But he denied it before them all: “I do not know what you are talking about.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was sitting in the courtyard.
A servant girl spoke to him.
She said he was with Jesus the Galilean.
Peter denied her words.
He spoke in front of everyone.
He said, "I do not know what you are talking about."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο ἔμπροσθεν πάντων λέγων Οὐκ οἶδα τί λέγεις

passages.text: When Peter had gone out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter left the courtyard.
Peter went to the gateway.
Another servant girl saw Peter.
She spoke to the people who were there.
She said, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth."
passages.original: Ἐξελθόντα δὲ εἰς τὸν πυλῶνα εἶδεν αὐτὸν ἄλλη καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἐκεῖ Οὗτος ἦν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου

passages.text: And again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man!”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
\r\nPeter spoke to the people near him.
\r\nPeter denied knowing Jesus.
\r\nPeter made an oath.
\r\nPeter said, “I do not know the man.”
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἠρνήσατο μετὰ ὅρκου ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: After a little while, those standing nearby came up to Peter. “Surely you are one of them,” they said, “for your accent gives you away.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus of Nazareth.
He stood near the gateway.
Some people stood nearby.
After a little while, these people came up to Peter.
They spoke to Peter.
They said, “Surely you are one of them.”
They meant Peter was one of Jesus’ followers.
They said, “Your accent gives you away.”
They recognized Peter’s way of speaking.
They believed Peter was with Jesus.
passages.original: Μετὰ μικρὸν δὲ προσελθόντες οἱ ἑστῶτες εἶπον τῷ Πέτρῳ Ἀληθῶς καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ καὶ γὰρ ἡ λαλιά σου δῆλόν σε ποιεῖ

passages.text: At that he began to curse and swear to them, “I do not know the man!” And immediately a rooster crowed.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter stood among people who questioned him.
Peter began to curse.
Peter swore an oath to them.
Peter said, “I do not know the man.”
Immediately, a rooster crowed.
passages.original: Τότε ἤρξατο καταθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύειν ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον Καὶ εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν

passages.text: Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” And he went outside and wept bitterly.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter had just denied knowing Jesus three times.
A rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had said.
Jesus had told Peter, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
Peter went outside.
Peter wept bitterly.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ῥήματος Ἰησοῦ εἰρηκότος ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς
